scope: Joint weak-bend reaction and actual tag motion on one open strip, with a compressed native-cell energy test on a measured material snapshot.
assumptions: First-order transverse response about an open Morse row. Nine registered wall contacts share each section position. The scalar twelve-site material response has unit drag and a common orientationally averaged site law. Like sites in adjacent sections have positive reference shear times local order; weak bends can change axial forces starting at second order. External traction uses the inherited four-dimensional axisymmetric carrier and order fields. The native snapshot trial replaces inter-section shear with strained triangular Morse bonds; wall and exterior offsets are fixed in the perturbation.

reviews.verbatim: Scoped clear for the joint weak-bend force and material transit clocks of the open strip with order-weighted reference shear.
reviews.limit: Method review. Neutral shear continued into the compressed material is a constitutive hypothesis. The work check is instantaneous at fixed geometry.

reviews.verbatim: Scoped clear for the conditional signed wall reactions and measured material clocks, and for a constrained negative-curvature witness on the reconstructed nearest-neighbor triangular snapshots.
reviews.limit: Verified ten guarded runs, tag timestamps, force ratios, inventories, and centered energy test. Nine trial displacements are not nine independent eigenmodes. Dynamics after rearrangement and free-mouth acceleration remain open.
